# 2 Baruch Chapter 30 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 2 Baruch Chapter 30 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 30:2 — "in hope of him / trusting in him"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "in-the-hope of-him" | Literal: Syriac b-sabreh = in his hope |
| LOGOS | "in hope of him" | Formal equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "trusting in him" | Interprets hope as trust/faith |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained LOGOS "in hope of him." The Syriac term is "hope" (sabra), not "trust" (haymanutha). PNEUMA's interpretation, while theologically close, changes the specific term.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 30:2 — "go forth / pour out / come forth"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "they-will-come-forth" | Literal exit from treasury |
| LOGOS | "they will go forth" | Formal equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "they will pour out" | Vivid, emphasizes multitude |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "they will go forth." Both EMET and LOGOS use the same Syriac verb (npaq = go out/come forth). PNEUMA's "pour out" is evocative but not textually supported.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 30:5 — "perdition / destruction"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "their-perdition-has-arrived" | Perdition = theological term for final ruin |
| LOGOS | "their perdition has arrived" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "their destruction is upon them" | More accessible modern term |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained EMET/LOGOS "perdition." The word carries appropriate eschatological weight and is the standard rendering of the Syriac 'abadana in this context.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS. Theological register.

---
